sections.heading: What is different about a Troy claim

c.v: Michigan’s auto insurance system affects how an injury claim arising from a Troy crash is handled. Under MCL 500.3009, the default bodily injury liability limits are $250,000 per person and $500,000 per accident, although qualifying drivers may elect lower limits. Personal injury protection (PIP) benefits generally cover eligible medical expenses and wage loss regardless of fault, subject to Michigan’s priority rules, selected coverage limits, and applicable exclusions. A claim against an at-fault driver may provide additional compensation. Certain non-economic damages require a qualifying threshold injury under MCL 500.3135. The available insurance limits, responsible parties, and recoverable damages must be evaluated separately. Uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage may provide additional protection when an at-fault driver has insufficient insurance or no applicable liability insurance. These benefits depend on the specific policy terms, including any notice, consent-to-settle, exhaustion, or other contractual requirements. Before accepting a settlement, it is important to review all potentially applicable coverage. See our

Roads in and around Troy may be maintained by the City of Troy, the Road Commission for Oakland County, or the Michigan Department of Transportation, depending on the location. I-75 and I-696 are state highways, while responsibility for other roads and intersections must be verified individually. Governmental agencies are generally protected by immunity, subject to statutory exceptions. Michigan’s highway exception, MCL 691.1402, may permit qualifying claims involving a failure to maintain a highway in reasonable repair. However, claims involving traffic signals, road signs, or visibility conditions do not automatically fall within that exception. Under MCL 691.1404, a person pursuing a qualifying highway-defect claim generally must provide written notice within 120 days of the injury, subject to specific statutory exceptions. Claims against the state may also involve Court of Claims procedures under MCL 600.6431. Determining the responsible agency and the applicable notice requirements promptly is important.

Accidents involving publicly owned vehicles, including police vehicles, fire vehicles, school buses, public transit buses, and municipal maintenance trucks, may raise questions under Michigan’s governmental immunity laws. MCL 691.1405 provides an exception involving negligent operation of government-owned motor vehicles. Whether the exception applies depends on the vehicle, the conduct, and the circumstances of the collision. See our
The 52-4 District Court and Sixth Judicial Circuit Court.

The 52nd District Court, Fourth Division, is located at 520 W. Big Beaver Road and serves Troy and Clawson. It generally handles civil disputes involving $25,000 or less, including qualifying mini-tort vehicle-damage claims. Larger civil injury lawsuits arising in Oakland County may be heard in the Sixth Judicial Circuit Court in Pontiac, provided the court and venue requirements are satisfied. Wrongful death cases may also require probate proceedings for estate administration, and certain settlements involving minors require court approval. When an accident occurs near the Oakland–Macomb county boundary, the proper court depends on Michigan’s jurisdiction and venue rules, including MCL 600.1629.

People injured in Troy may receive treatment at Corewell Health Beaumont Troy Hospital, located at 44201 Dequindre Road, or at other hospitals serving Oakland County. Corewell Health William Beaumont University Hospital in Royal Oak is a Level I adult trauma center. Medical records, diagnostic imaging, treatment notes, and available emergency medical services documentation can become important evidence in an injury claim.

faqs.question: Where are the crashes in Troy?

answer.v: Troy’s major traffic corridors include I-75, Big Beaver Road, Rochester Road, Crooks Road, Maple Road, and Fourteen Mile Road. These roads carry commuter, retail, and commercial traffic, and crashes can occur at intersections, freeway entrances, and business driveways. According to Michigan Traffic Crash Facts, Oakland County recorded 35,951 crashes, 9,139 injuries, and 68 fatalities in 2024.

faqs.question: I was hurt because of a signal problem or road defect on Big Beaver or Rochester. Who do I claim against?

answer.v: The responsible governmental agency depends on the precise location and nature of the condition. Different agencies may maintain the roadway and its traffic-control devices. Governmental immunity also limits which claims can proceed. For a qualifying highway-defect claim, Michigan law generally requires written notice within 120 days under MCL 691.1404. An attorney can investigate the responsible agency, applicable immunity exception, and notice requirements.

faqs.question: The other driver’s insurer offered their $250,000 policy limit. Should I take it?

answer.v: Not before checking your own underinsured motorist coverage and getting your insurer’s written consent to settle. Accepting the liability limit without consent can forfeit the UIM claim under most policies. A lawyer can sequence the two claims so you recover both.

faqs.question: I fell at Somerset or in a Big Beaver office tower. Who is responsible?

answer.v: Potentially responsible parties may include the property owner, property manager, or a contractor responsible for the dangerous condition. Liability depends on who owed a legal duty, whether that duty was breached, and whether the breach caused the injury. In Kandil-Elsayed v F & E Oil, Inc. (2023), the Michigan Supreme Court held that an open and obvious hazard does not automatically eliminate a property possessor’s duty to an invitee. The condition may remain relevant to breach and comparative fault. Photographs, incident reports, witness information, and available surveillance footage can be important evidence. If the injury occurred in the course of employment, workers' compensation or a separate third-party claim may also be relevant.

faqs.question: Where would my Troy injury case be filed?

answer.v: Claims up to $25,000, including mini tort claims, in the 52-4 District Court on Big Beaver; injury suits over $25,000 in the Sixth Judicial Circuit Court in Pontiac.

faqs.question: I was treated at Corewell Health Troy and something went wrong. Is that a malpractice case?

answer.v: Possibly. Medical malpractice has a two-year deadline with a six-month discovery rule, a mandatory 182-day notice of intent before suit (MCL 600.2912b), an affidavit of merit, and the noneconomic damage caps in MCL 600.1483 ($596,400 for 2026, or $1,065,000 for the most severe injuries). Cases are expert-driven and screened carefully.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to hire you?

answer.v: Nothing up front, and no fee unless we recover money for you. Michigan caps contingency fees in personal injury cases at one-third of the recovery (MCR 8.121).
